analysis.title: GWIS: Buy the GS China Go-Global Biotech basket ahead of catalysts
key_insights: Graham Ambrose (GS FICC & Equities, not Global Investment Research) recommends buying the GS China Go-Global Biotech basket (GSXACBIO) ahead of catalysts. The basket holds 15 companies, averages US$100m/day in liquidity and trades on 25x 12/27 PE.

Wuxi Apptech (US$70bn market cap) has doubled this year and is now a top-10 holding among China onshore mutual funds as of 3Q, alongside major technology names. The note says fundamentals remain on an upward trajectory.
The GS China Healthcare team hosted management teams from 70+ Asia healthcare companies at the November Corporate Day. The note says the debate has shifted from re-entry to positioning for 2027.

China's leading biotechs are moving from domestic innovators to globally validated oncology leaders. Near-term performance is driven by US FDA milestones, multi-regional late-stage trial readouts and global commercial rollouts backed by multinational pharma partners.
Basket weights named: BeOne 21%, Innovent 19%, Akeso 13%, Zai Lab 5%, Kelun 5%.

Ivonescimab (Akeso / Summit Therapeutics) faces an imminent FDA decision in patients with genetically mutated lung cancer whose disease progressed after initial targeted therapy. HARMONi-3 global trial results in squamous lung cancer will determine whether it can displace current global standards of care.

Zai Lab's Zoci targets extensive-stage small cell lung cancer and rare neuroendocrine tumors. A global Phase 3 registrational trial in first-line small cell lung cancer is to start by year-end 2026, and neuroendocrine tumor expansion-study topline results are expected in 1H 2027.

BeOne Medicines (formerly BeiGene) is the basket's commercial anchor, with over $5.3 billion in 2025 revenue led by blood cancers. Late-stage gastrointestinal and breast cancer trials are advancing toward international regulatory submissions.
Innovent is moving from upfront licensing payments to development milestones and eventual royalties through late-stage collaborations with partners such as Takeda.

Kelun's Sac-TMT (partnered with Merck MSD) has global Phase 3 readouts across 2027 in stomach, lung and hormone-driven breast cancer. Positive readouts would support international filings under Kelun's multi-billion dollar partnership with Merck.
November Corp Day takeaway: CDMO (contract drug development and manufacturing) is still preferred into 2027, and opportunities are broadening.
The author calls selecting individual winners 'a bit of a casino', which is the case for using the basket. The basket can be adjusted to include or exclude names.
